title: What if you stood on a scale on Jupiter?
caption:
Jupiter would more than double your weight. ⚖️🪐

Jupiter's pull is 2.36× Earth's (NASA), so a 70 kg person would see about 165 kg on the scale.

The same scale reads about 26 kg on Mars and about 12 kg on the Moon.

Catch: Jupiter has no solid ground. Its "surface gravity" is measured at the 1-bar level of its atmosphere.

The twist: Saturn has 95× Earth's mass, yet you'd weigh less there (0.92×, about 64 kg) because it is so wide.

Send this to the friend who always blames the scale.

Tomorrow: ice cream on Mercury.

⚠️ Don't try this. Piling on weights to "feel Jupiter" can injure your back and knees.
